title: Revision groups gave no clear gain in NHC 48-hour wind error bands in two basins in 2019-2025
abstract: We tested the size of a 24-hour same-valid-time wind forecast revision as an uncertainty predictor for NHC forecasts. Each target year in 2019-2025 used only the previous five years. Fixed revision groups set Gaussian means and spreads for 90% error bands. At 48 hours, the conditional-minus-pooled interval score was -0.21 kt (95% whole-storm limits -1.83 to +1.50) for 1,202 Atlantic cycles and +1.02 kt (-0.31 to +2.66) for 733 East Pacific cycles. Neither primary comparison showed a clear gain. An exploratory large-to-small revision mean squared error ratio was 2.06 (1.27-3.03) in the Atlantic and 0.92 (0.56-1.46) in the East Pacific. The Atlantic relation did not transfer to the second basin in this sample. One secondary 24-hour Atlantic test gave a gain, but its East Pacific test did not. Revised records, matched-case selection, fixed-fit uncertainty and seven test years limit inference. These are constructed bands, not issued NHC probabilities. Code, source hashes, aggregate evidence and an independent numerical check support reproduction.

display.caption: Closed 90% error-band coverage by absolute revision in matched 48-hour forecasts for 2019-2025. These are constructed bands, not issued probabilities.
